Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is 9to5Mac's weekly column dedicated to the latest apps in the indie app scene. If you're a developer and want to feature your app, feel free to contact us anytime.

Farwave takes an interesting new approach to designing a music player, placing radio stations on a globe. You can explore the world, search for radio stations from around the globe, and enjoy stunning 3D visuals. The podcasts and music you want to listen to can also be browsed with their own unique visual effects within the app.

Key Features

Farwave lets you listen to radio stations from all over the world. You can spin the globe, find a region, and tap on a station. If you want to listen to something randomly, there's also a "Take Me Anywhere" button. The app also keeps a listening history so you can revisit stations later.

Beyond radio, Farwave also offers podcasts and music, each displayed on its own planetary interface. You can search for podcasts or add their RSS feeds, and the app also supports playlists, playback speed adjustment, and offline downloads.

For music, the app doesn't support Apple Music, but you can import your own music files from your computer or the Files app. Each artist has its own signal source, and music is stored on the device for offline playback.

Download the App

Farwave is available for free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad running iOS 18 or later. For the full experience, including podcasts, music import, and more, you can subscribe to FarWave Pro for $2.99 per month or $14.99 per year.
